name: The Joint Commission & CHAI — Guidance on the Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH)
quote: When appropriate, patients should be notified when AI directly impacts their care and how their data may be used in the context of AI.
quote_label: Joint Commission & Coalition for Health AI, Guidance on the Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH), §2 Patient Privacy and Transparency (©2025)

provenance.note: Stuck pending since 2026-08-30 (missed its NEW week); coded this run. Segment gap (healthcare accreditor). D1=1: organizational monitoring and auditing ('regularly monitoring and/or auditing AI systems to identify and address biases'), AI incidents captured 'like patient safety events', but no decision-level record. D2=1: 'governance creates accountability'; 'a designated individual(s) focused on AI quality/safety-related issues'; no clinician sign-off on AI outputs. D3=1: notification is qualified ('When appropriate'), consent 'Where and when relevant'. D4=0: none. D5=1: human judgment named only in rationale ('emphasizes the importance of keeping humans in the decision-making process'; risk that 'overreliance on AI could potentially diminish the role of human judgment'); no required human review step. D6=2: local validation, bias evaluation before and after deployment, risk-based post-deployment monitoring. Posture Enabling: written to 'fully harness the transformative potential of AI' across diagnosis, treatment planning and administration. c2_fit=partially: draws no permit-vs-reserve line by task; the governing variable is organizational risk ('risk-based and scaled to your setting'), not proof cost — scope covers 'decision support, diagnosis, treatment planning' with the same guardrails as scheduling. c3=Evidential.
